title: SDK artifact attestation and cross-registry publish flow (PyPI / npm / Go modules)
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Implement an end-to-end artifact attestation and publish flow for Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Goals: 1) produce deterministic, provenance-bearing artifacts (wheels/tarballs, npm packages, go modules), 2) sign and attest artifacts using Sigstore + in-toto where possible, 3) extend CI to perform reproducible builds and cross-registry publishes, 4) add lightweight runtime verification helpers in each SDK so enterprise customers can validate signatures locally. This ticket covers CI pipelines, release matrix changes, registry credentials handling, and adding examples demonstrating verification. Coordination needed with SDK maintainers to ensure packaging changes do not alter runtime behavior (esp. streaming ergonomics and retry wrappers).
comments: 2025-02-14 — Priya: Created ticket after workshop with SDK leads; initial scope drafted. Decided to aim for Sigstore + in-toto for primary attestation; fallback options for legacy registries noted.

2025-02-18 — Ethan: Spike completed — prototype using Sigstore (cosign + rekor) to sign Python wheels produced in a PEP 517 build. Observed nondeterministic metadata in sdist producing different checksums across runners. Need build isolation and pinned build-environments (manylinux tag + reproducible-build flags).

2025-02-25 — Marco Alvarez (review): Reviewed prototype. Recommend adding a canonical build step using docker container built from pinned Dockerfile and storing the image digest in the in-toto link. Raised question about npm package signing; proposal to use sigstore for npm + npm's publish token flow rather than GPG-based signing.

2025-02-27 — Priya: Decided trade-offs: accept ~3-6 minute CI overhead for attestation generation in exchange for enterprise compliance. Plan: 1) canonical build container per language, 2) produce in-toto link metadata, 3) cosign sign the artifact and upload to registry with attestation to rekor.

2025-03-03 — Ethan: Integration tests failing for Go modules when using module proxy because timestamp ordering affects go.sum. Added normalize step to strip build timestamps and verified determinism for the test suite. Next: wire credentials via vault and test cross-account publish to npm registry in staging.

2025-03-05 — Priya: Added verification helper snippets into sdk-python and @redwood/sdk-js repos (proof-of-concept). Open questions: UX for SDKs to validate at runtime vs. offline verification; recommend offline-first with optional runtime check in debug builds.
